_meta.keyKnowledge: We are learning about the Australian taxation system and how the revenue from taxes is used to fund public services.

toLevel2.question: Income tax in Australia has no link to any income earned through wages or salary in any year of operation today.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax is paid on income earned by a person across the financial year through wages or salary.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating income tax as unlinked to wages and salary misstates Australian taxation at this level.

toLevel2.question: Tax revenue in Australia has no link to any public service that any government funds in any year of operation.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue funds public services such as health, education, defence, and infrastructure across Australia.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating tax revenue as unrelated to services misstates a core function of taxation.

toLevel2.question: The Goods and Services Tax has no link to the price of any goods or services in any Australian shop in any year today.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The GST is a tax added to the price of most goods and services sold in Australia.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating the GST as unrelated to retail prices misstates how the tax operates in Australia.

toLevel2.question: Higher earners under a progressive income tax system always pay a lower percentage in tax than lower earners do.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Higher earners under a progressive income tax system pay a higher percentage in tax than lower earners do.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating progressive tax as taxing higher earners less reverses the basic concept.

toLevel2.question: Company tax in Australia has no link to any profits earned by companies across any financial year of operation.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Company tax is a tax paid by companies on profits earned across the financial year.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating company tax as unlinked to profits misstates how the tax operates in Australia.

toLevel2.question: Capital gains tax is paid on profits made when selling certain assets such as shares or investment property.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Capital gains tax is paid on profits from selling certain assets such as shares or investment property.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the standard description of capital gains tax at this level.

toLevel2.question: Government budgets balance the need for tax revenue with the desire to keep taxes low for households and businesses.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Government budgets balance the need for revenue with the desire to keep taxes low for households and businesses.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is widely taught as a core feature of budget decisions at this level.

toLevel2.question: Tax revenue in Australia has no link to schools, hospitals, or roads in any state at any stage of any year today.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue funds schools, hospitals, and roads in many parts of Australia each year.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating tax revenue as unrelated to public infrastructure misstates a core function of taxation.

toLevel2.question: A simplified government budget shows where tax revenue comes from and where it is spent across major service areas.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A simplified government budget shows where tax revenue comes from and where it is spent across major areas.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is widely taught as a tool for understanding government finance at this level.

toLevel2.question: Tax literacy is irrelevant to young people because no Australian under twenty-five ever earns any income at any time.
toLevel2.correct: False
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Many Australians earn income before the age of twenty-five, so tax literacy is relevant to young people.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating young Australians as never earning income misstates real working patterns at this level.

toLevel2.question: Income tax, GST, company tax, and capital gains tax are all forms of tax used in the Australian taxation system.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax, GST, company tax, and capital gains tax are all forms of tax in the Australian taxation system.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: These four forms of tax are widely taught at this level.

toLevel2.question: Understanding how taxation works helps young Australians take part in informed debates about government spending choices.
toLevel2.correct: True
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Understanding taxation supports informed debate about government spending choices among young Australians.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is a recognised goal at this level for tax literacy.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes income tax in Australia?
toLevel2.correct: A tax paid on income earned by a person through wages, salary, or other taxable earnings across the financial year
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax is paid on income earned by a person through wages, salary, or other taxable earnings.

distractors.answer: A tax paid on every product bought from any Australian shop without any link to a person's income at all
distractors.explanation: A tax on products is the GST, not income tax.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only by overseas tourists when they visit Australia for any holiday at any stage of any year today
distractors.explanation: Income tax applies to many residents who earn income, not only tourists.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only by children for completing chores at home each weekend across every year of their childhood
distractors.explanation: Children's chore payments are not income tax.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes the GST in Australia?
toLevel2.correct: A tax added to the price of most goods and services sold in Australia at a set percentage rate
toLevel2.correctExplanation: The GST is a tax added to the price of most goods and services sold in Australia.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only by Australian companies on profits earned across the financial year in any sector
distractors.explanation: A tax on company profits is company tax, not GST.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only on capital gains from selling assets like shares or investment property each year
distractors.explanation: A tax on profits from selling assets is capital gains tax, not GST.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only by children for completing chores at home each weekend across every year of life
distractors.explanation: Children's chore payments are not the GST.

toLevel2.question: What is progressive income tax?
toLevel2.correct: A system where the tax rate rises as a person's taxable income rises across the financial year
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Progressive income tax means the tax rate rises as taxable income rises across the year.

distractors.answer: A system where every earner pays exactly the same percentage of income regardless of their total earnings today
distractors.explanation: A flat-rate system would tax all earners at the same percentage; that is not progressive tax.

distractors.answer: A system where higher earners pay a smaller percentage of income than lower earners do across every year
distractors.explanation: Higher earners paying less is the opposite of progressive tax.

distractors.answer: A system where the government pays every earner a salary regardless of any income earned at any time today
distractors.explanation: Government salary payments are not what progressive income tax describes.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is a public service typically funded by Australian tax revenue?
toLevel2.correct: Public hospitals, public schools, defence forces, and major roads built and maintained across the country
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Public hospitals, schools, defence forces, and major roads are typically funded by Australian tax revenue.

distractors.answer: Office wall colours, free public concerts, and other items unrelated to government spending in any year today
distractors.explanation: Office colours and free concerts are not public services in this sense.

distractors.answer: A single private business in one suburb of one Australian city in any single year of the country's history
distractors.explanation: A single private business is not a publicly funded service.

distractors.answer: A child's pocket money paid by a parent for tidying a bedroom each Saturday morning across every year of life
distractors.explanation: Children's chore pocket money is not a publicly funded service.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes company tax in Australia?
toLevel2.correct: A tax paid by Australian companies on profits earned across the financial year at a set percentage rate
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Company tax is paid by Australian companies on profits earned across the financial year.

distractors.answer: A tax paid by every consumer on every product purchased from any shop in any state in any year today
distractors.explanation: A consumer tax on products is the GST, not company tax.

distractors.answer: A tax paid by every individual person on every dollar of wages earned across every year of their life
distractors.explanation: An individual tax on wages is income tax, not company tax.

distractors.answer: A tax paid by every Australian on every meal eaten in any household in any year of life at every stage
distractors.explanation: There is no Australian tax on every household meal.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes capital gains tax?
toLevel2.correct: A tax paid on profits made when selling certain assets such as shares or investment property in Australia
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Capital gains tax is paid on profits from selling certain assets such as shares or investment property.

distractors.answer: A tax paid on every product purchased from any Australian shop without any link to any asset sale today
distractors.explanation: A tax on products is the GST, not capital gains tax.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only by Australian companies on profits earned across the financial year in any sector at all
distractors.explanation: A tax on company profits is company tax, not capital gains tax.

distractors.answer: A tax paid only on income earned through wages or salary across the financial year in any year today
distractors.explanation: A tax on wages or salary is income tax, not capital gains tax.

toLevel2.question: Why does the Australian government collect tax revenue?
toLevel2.correct: To fund public services such as health, education, defence, and infrastructure across the country each year
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax revenue funds public services such as health, education, defence, and infrastructure across the country.

distractors.answer: To set the price of every product in every Australian shop in every state in every year of trading today
distractors.explanation: Governments do not set product prices in markets through tax revenue.

distractors.answer: To run a single private business in one suburb without any link to any public service in any year ever today
distractors.explanation: Governments fund public services with tax revenue, not a private suburb business.

distractors.answer: To pay every Australian a fixed weekly salary regardless of whether they ever work or earn any income today
distractors.explanation: Tax revenue does not pay every Australian a fixed weekly salary regardless of work.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following best describes a simplified government budget?
toLevel2.correct: A document showing where tax revenue comes from and where it is spent across major service and capital areas
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A simplified government budget shows where tax revenue comes from and where it is spent across major areas.

distractors.answer: A document showing only the colour of office walls in every government building across the country today
distractors.explanation: Office colours are not what a budget document covers.

distractors.answer: A document showing only the lunch menu in every government cafeteria across every state in every year
distractors.explanation: Lunch menus are not what a government budget document covers.

distractors.answer: A document showing only the names of every public servant employed in any government department today
distractors.explanation: Names of every public servant are not the focus of a simplified budget document.

toLevel2.question: Which of the following is the best example of progressive income tax in action?
toLevel2.correct: A worker on $200,000 pays a higher percentage of income in tax than a worker on $40,000 across the same year
toLevel2.correctExplanation: A higher earner paying a higher percentage in tax than a lower earner is progressive income tax in action.

distractors.answer: A worker on $200,000 pays exactly the same percentage of income in tax as a worker on $40,000 across the same year
distractors.explanation: Identical percentages across earners describe a flat tax, not progressive tax.

distractors.answer: A worker on $40,000 pays a higher percentage of income in tax than a worker on $200,000 across the same year
distractors.explanation: A lower earner paying a higher percentage is the opposite of progressive tax.

distractors.answer: A worker on $200,000 pays no income tax at all while a worker on $40,000 pays a high percentage of income
distractors.explanation: Higher earners paying no tax at all is not how progressive tax works.

toLevel2.question: Which list includes only forms of tax used in the Australian taxation system?
toLevel2.correct: Income tax, GST, company tax, capital gains tax, and other taxes used by Australian governments today
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Income tax, GST, company tax, and capital gains tax are all forms of tax used in the Australian taxation system.

distractors.answer: Office wall colours, free public concerts, and other items unrelated to taxation in any country at any time
distractors.explanation: Office colours and free concerts are not forms of tax.

distractors.answer: A single private fee paid by one person in one suburb in one year of one decade in one Australian state today
distractors.explanation: A private fee paid in one suburb is not a national form of tax.

distractors.answer: Random outcomes and fixed amounts by chance with no link to any tax in any country at any stage of any year today
distractors.explanation: Random outcomes and fixed amounts by chance are not how tax works.

toLevel2.question: Why does a government balance the need for tax revenue with the desire to keep taxes low?
toLevel2.correct: Higher taxes raise more revenue but can affect households and businesses, so governments balance both pressures together
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Higher taxes raise more revenue but affect households and businesses; governments balance both pressures.

distractors.answer: Higher taxes have no link to households or businesses in any country in any year at any stage of life today
distractors.explanation: Higher taxes are closely linked to households and businesses.

distractors.answer: Higher taxes always raise less revenue than lower taxes in every country in every year at every stage of trading
distractors.explanation: Higher taxes usually raise more revenue, not less, in standard analysis.

distractors.answer: Higher taxes always remove every choice from every government in every country in every year today at every stage
distractors.explanation: Tax decisions involve real choices for governments, not the removal of choice.

toLevel2.question: Why is tax literacy useful for young Australians as they begin to earn income?
toLevel2.correct: It helps a young person understand pay slips, tax returns, and how their tax revenue funds public services they use
toLevel2.correctExplanation: Tax literacy helps a young person understand pay slips, tax returns, and how tax revenue funds public services.

distractors.answer: It has no link to any pay slip or tax return for any young Australian in any year at any stage of life today
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy is closely linked to pay slips and tax returns.

distractors.answer: It always guarantees that a young Australian will pay no income tax at any stage of their working life today
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy supports understanding; it does not eliminate income tax for the worker.

distractors.answer: It always removes every choice from a young Australian about study, training, or career across every year today
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy expands rather than removes choice.

toLevel3.question: A worker earning $40,000 a year and a worker earning $200,000 a year usually pay different amounts of income tax in Australia.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A $40,000 earner and a $200,000 earner usually pay different amounts of income tax under the progressive system.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the basic outcome of a progressive income tax system at this level.

toLevel3.question: GST has no link to the final price a consumer pays for most goods and services in any Australian shop today.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: GST is added to the price of most goods and services and is part of the final price a consumer pays.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating GST as unlinked to final prices misstates how the tax operates in Australia.

toLevel3.question: A government that increases health spending has no link to any need to raise revenue or reduce other spending today.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A health spending increase usually requires more revenue or less spending elsewhere because budgets are limited.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating health spending as unlinked to revenue or other spending misstates budget trade-offs at this level.

toLevel3.question: A simplified government budget has no link to where tax revenue comes from in any state at any stage of any year today.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A simplified government budget shows where tax revenue comes from across major sources such as income tax and GST.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating budgets as unlinked to tax revenue sources misstates a core feature of budget documents.

toLevel3.question: Capital gains tax in Australia applies only to profits from selling certain assets, not to wages from a normal job.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Capital gains tax applies to profits from selling certain assets, not to wages earned in a normal job.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the standard distinction between capital gains tax and income tax at this level.

toLevel3.question: Public services such as Medicare and public schools have no link to any tax revenue in any year of operation today.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Public services such as Medicare and public schools rely on tax revenue for their core funding each year.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating these services as unlinked to tax revenue misstates how Australian governments fund public services.

toLevel3.question: Progressive income tax in Australia means the tax rate rises as a person's taxable income rises across the year.
toLevel3.correct: True
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Progressive income tax means the tax rate rises as taxable income rises across the year.

distractors.answer: False
distractors.explanation: This is the standard description of progressive income tax at this level.

toLevel3.question: Reducing taxes always raises the amount of tax revenue a government collects across every year of every economy.
toLevel3.correct: False
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Reducing taxes usually lowers the tax revenue a government collects, though some specific tax cuts can grow other revenue over time.

distractors.answer: True
distractors.explanation: Treating tax cuts as always raising revenue misstates standard public finance at this level.

toLevel3.question: Mia earns $50,000 in a year and her father earns $150,000. Which idea best fits the income tax they pay under the progressive system in Australia?
toLevel3.correct: The father pays a higher percentage of income in tax than Mia because progressive tax rises with taxable income
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Under Australia's progressive tax system, the higher earner pays a higher percentage of income in tax.

distractors.answer: Mia and her father pay exactly the same percentage of income in tax because Australian tax is always flat across earners
distractors.explanation: Australian income tax is progressive, not flat.

distractors.answer: Mia pays a higher percentage of income in tax than her father because higher earners always pay less in any year today
distractors.explanation: Lower earners paying a higher percentage is the opposite of progressive tax.

distractors.answer: Mia and her father pay no income tax at all because Australian tax never applies to any individual at any stage of life
distractors.explanation: Many Australian individuals do pay income tax; the no-tax claim is wrong.

toLevel3.question: Jarrah buys a new pair of headphones from an Australian shop. Which idea best fits the GST on the purchase?
toLevel3.correct: The GST is added to the price of most goods and services sold in Australia at a set percentage rate
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The GST is added to the price of most goods and services sold in Australia at a set percentage rate.

distractors.answer: The GST is added only to luxury cars and never appears on the price of headphones in any Australian shop today
distractors.explanation: The GST applies to most goods and services, not only luxury cars.

distractors.answer: The GST is paid only by Australian companies on profits earned across the financial year in any sector at all
distractors.explanation: Company profit tax is company tax, not the GST.

distractors.answer: The GST is paid only by overseas tourists when they buy any product in any Australian shop in any state today
distractors.explanation: The GST applies to most consumer purchases in Australia, not only tourist purchases.

toLevel3.question: Anika reads about the Australian government raising health spending by $5 billion. Which idea best fits the trade-off this involves?
toLevel3.correct: The government must usually raise revenue or reduce other spending because budgets are limited and trade-offs apply
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The government must usually raise revenue or reduce other spending; budgets are limited and trade-offs apply.

distractors.answer: The government can fund every $5 billion increase without any change to any other area in any year of operation
distractors.explanation: Limited budgets force trade-offs; spending increases are not free of impact.

distractors.answer: The government has no link to any spending area because budgets and tax have no connection in any country today
distractors.explanation: Budgets and tax are closely linked; the no-link claim is wrong.

distractors.answer: The government always cuts its tax revenue when it raises spending in any sector at any stage of any year today
distractors.explanation: Tax revenue does not automatically fall when spending rises.

toLevel3.question: Sam reads a simplified government budget showing major sources of revenue. Which set best fits standard Australian sources?
toLevel3.correct: Income tax, GST, company tax, and capital gains tax together fund a large share of Australian government revenue
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Income tax, GST, company tax, and capital gains tax together fund a large share of Australian government revenue.

distractors.answer: Office cleaning fees, school fundraisers, and the price of stamps together fund a large share of revenue today
distractors.explanation: School fundraisers and stamp prices are not main sources of Australian government revenue.

distractors.answer: A single private fee paid in one suburb is the only source of Australian government revenue in every year today
distractors.explanation: Australian government revenue comes from many sources, not a single private fee.

distractors.answer: Random outcomes and fixed amounts by chance are the main sources of Australian government revenue each year
distractors.explanation: Government revenue comes from clear tax sources, not random outcomes.

toLevel3.question: Lila is told that 'Australian governments fund public services without any tax revenue at all'. Which response best fits the topic?
toLevel3.correct: The claim is misleading because tax revenue is the main source of funding for many Australian public services
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Tax revenue is the main source of funding for many Australian public services; the claim is misleading.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because tax revenue has no link to any public service in any state in any year today
distractors.explanation: Tax revenue is closely linked to many public services in Australia.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every public service in every Australian state always runs on private donations alone
distractors.explanation: Public services in Australia rely mainly on tax revenue, not only private donations.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because no Australian government has ever collected any tax revenue at any stage of history
distractors.explanation: Australian governments have collected tax revenue across many years.

toLevel3.question: Kofi reads about a person who sells investment property and makes a profit. Which Australian tax most directly applies to that profit?
toLevel3.correct: Capital gains tax, because it applies to profits from selling certain assets such as investment property in Australia
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Capital gains tax applies to profits from selling certain assets such as investment property in Australia.

distractors.answer: Income tax, because every dollar earned in any way is always taxed only as wages or salary income at all times today
distractors.explanation: Income tax applies to wages and salary, not directly to capital gains in this way.

distractors.answer: Company tax, because every individual sale of any asset is always taxed as a company profit in every year today
distractors.explanation: Company tax applies to companies, not to individual asset sales.

distractors.answer: GST, because every asset sold in any Australian setting always carries the GST regardless of any other tax today
distractors.explanation: GST applies to most goods and services, not directly to capital gains on assets.

toLevel3.question: Yen wants to compare a flat tax and a progressive tax at the same level of total revenue. Which idea best fits the comparison?
toLevel3.correct: A flat tax taxes every earner at the same rate, while a progressive tax taxes higher earners at a higher rate
toLevel3.correctExplanation: A flat tax taxes every earner at the same rate; a progressive tax taxes higher earners at a higher rate.

distractors.answer: A flat tax and a progressive tax are identical in every detail and never differ in any country at any stage today
distractors.explanation: Flat and progressive tax differ in how rates apply across earners.

distractors.answer: A flat tax always raises higher rates from lower earners than a progressive tax does across every country today
distractors.explanation: Flat tax does not always tax lower earners more; rates are equal in a flat tax.

distractors.answer: A flat tax and a progressive tax both tax only one earner across the whole country in every year today at all
distractors.explanation: Both systems apply across many earners, not only one in a country.

toLevel3.question: Rosa is asked why young Australians benefit from understanding the Australian taxation system. Which response best fits the topic?
toLevel3.correct: Tax literacy helps a young person understand pay slips, tax returns, and how taxes fund the public services they use
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Tax literacy helps a young person understand pay slips, tax returns, and how taxes fund public services.

distractors.answer: Tax literacy has no link to any pay slip or tax return for any young Australian in any year at any stage of life
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy is closely linked to pay slips and tax returns for many young workers.

distractors.answer: Tax literacy always guarantees that a young Australian will pay no income tax at any stage of their working life
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy supports understanding; it does not eliminate income tax.

distractors.answer: Tax literacy always removes every choice from a young Australian about study, training, or career across every year
distractors.explanation: Tax literacy expands rather than removes choice.

toLevel3.question: Amir reads about a debate over raising the Medicare levy to fund extra hospital services. Which idea best fits the debate?
toLevel3.correct: The debate weighs the benefit of extra hospital services against the cost to households of paying a higher levy
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The debate weighs the benefit of extra hospital services against the cost to households of paying a higher levy.

distractors.answer: The debate has no link to any hospital service or any household in any country at any stage of any year today
distractors.explanation: The debate is closely linked to hospital services and household budgets.

distractors.answer: The debate always ends in identical decisions across every Australian state in every year of operation today at all
distractors.explanation: Different debates lead to different decisions across states and years.

distractors.answer: The debate always removes every choice from every household and every government in every region in every year
distractors.explanation: Tax debates involve real choices for households and governments.

toLevel3.question: Jade looks at a simplified government budget. Which idea best fits how she should read the spending side of the budget?
toLevel3.correct: The spending side shows how tax revenue is allocated to areas like health, education, defence, and infrastructure
toLevel3.correctExplanation: The spending side shows how tax revenue is allocated to areas like health, education, defence, and infrastructure.

distractors.answer: The spending side has no link to any service in any country at any stage of any year of any government in any state
distractors.explanation: The spending side is closely linked to public services and infrastructure.

distractors.answer: The spending side always shows only one item in every government budget in every state at every stage today at all
distractors.explanation: The spending side covers many areas, not a single item.

distractors.answer: The spending side always lists every item by random draw with no link to any policy in any country at any time
distractors.explanation: Spending allocations reflect policy choices, not random draws.

toLevel3.question: Linh wants to calculate approximate income tax on a $60,000 salary using a simplified progressive table. Which idea best fits her approach?
toLevel3.correct: She applies different tax rates to different income brackets and adds the results to estimate total income tax due
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Progressive tax tables apply different rates to different income brackets, summed to estimate total tax.

distractors.answer: She multiplies the salary by a single rate that applies to every dollar of every salary in every Australian year today
distractors.explanation: A single rate across all dollars is a flat tax, not a progressive tax.

distractors.answer: She refuses to calculate any tax and assumes that the salary is always tax-free in every Australian setting today
distractors.explanation: Income on a salary is not tax-free; income tax usually applies.

distractors.answer: She adds the salary to the GST and treats the total as the only tax owed by the worker in any year today at all
distractors.explanation: Income tax and GST are different taxes that should not be added together this way.

toLevel3.question: Marcus reads that a government uses tax revenue to maintain major roads and railways. Which idea best fits this use of revenue?
toLevel3.correct: Infrastructure spending is a major use of tax revenue and supports the wider economy through transport and freight
toLevel3.correctExplanation: Infrastructure spending is a major use of tax revenue and supports the wider economy through transport and freight.

distractors.answer: Infrastructure spending has no link to any road or railway in any country at any stage of any year of operation today
distractors.explanation: Infrastructure spending is closely linked to roads and railways.

distractors.answer: Infrastructure spending is funded only by private companies and never receives any tax revenue from any government
distractors.explanation: Many roads and railways receive substantial tax revenue, not only private funding.
